title: Two reads from one index
starter:
%d   = buffer 8 [1 2 3 4 10 20 30 40] dtype=i32 slot=0
%ix  = buffer 1 [2] dtype=i32 slot=1
%res = buffer 1 dtype=i32 slot=2
%i0  = shrink %ix 0 []
%i   = load %i0

samples.label:
buffer slot 0 starts as [1 2 3 4 10 20 30 40]
buffer slot 1 starts as [2]
final contents of slot 2

buffer slot 0 starts as [1 2 3 4 10 20 30 40]
buffer slot 1 starts as [5]
final contents of slot 2

buffer slot 0 starts as [1 2 3 4 10 20 30 40]
buffer slot 1 starts as [-1]
final contents of slot 2

hints: Start by shaping the index: `%k = mod %i 4` has bounds `[0, 3]`. Every offset you need can be built from `%k`.
The first read is `shrink %d %k []`. For the second, make the offset its own line: `%o = add %k 4` has bounds `[4, 7]`, and the last allowed start of a one-element view on 8 elements is 7.
Load both views, `add` the two values, then write the sum the way lesson 2.2 did: `shrink %res 0 []`, a `store` into that view, and `after %res` with the store.

answer.code:
%d   = buffer 8 [1 2 3 4 10 20 30 40] dtype=i32 slot=0
%ix  = buffer 1 [2] dtype=i32 slot=1
%res = buffer 1 dtype=i32 slot=2
%i0  = shrink %ix 0 []
%i   = load %i0
%k   = mod %i 4
%a0  = shrink %d %k []
%a   = load %a0
%o   = add %k 4
%b0  = shrink %d %o []
%b   = load %b0
%v   = add %a %b
%r0  = shrink %res 0 []
%s   = store %r0 %v
%r1  = after %res %s
answer.explain: `mod %i 4` is in `[0, 3]` for every loaded `%i`, so `shrink %d %k []` is proven. `add %k 4` adds the ends: `[4, 7]`, which still fits inside `[0, 7]`, so the second view is proven too. Both proofs hold before the program runs and for any data in `ix`. The rest is a store and an `after`, as in lesson 2.2.
